## Root cause
It turns out that these permits, along with a few others, were generated before the fix in [this commit](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/permit-generation/commit/e4e8eaef1d065cffdcb379b001c62d0fa971010e):
The issue was originally fixed in this diff:
```diff
 const { domain, types, values } = SignatureTransfer.getPermitData(permitTransferFromData, PERMIT2_ADDRESS, evmNetworkId);
-  const domainData = {
-    name: domain.name,
-    version: domain.version || "1", //  default to 1 if it's undefined
-    chainId: domain.chainId,
-    verifyingContract: domain.verifyingContract,
-  };
  try {
-    const signature = await adminWallet._signTypedData(domainData, types, values);
+    const signature = await adminWallet._signTypedData(domain, types, values);
    const erc20Permit: PermitReward = {
      tokenType: TokenType.ERC20,
```
## Description
The Permit2 contract utilizes EIP-712 [Domain Separators](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712#definition-of-domainseparator) to mitigate replay attacks.
The above `domainData` used to generate these permits included a `version` field, which is optional in the EIP-712 standard. This field was not used in the Permit2 protocol, as seen in its [implementation](https://github.com/Uniswap/permit2/blob/main/src/EIP712.sol) and the [deployed version](https://gnosisscan.io/address/0x000000000022d473030f116ddee9f6b43ac78ba3#code#F10#L1).  
Attempting to claim these invalid permits leads to an `UNPREDICTABLE_GAS_LIMIT` error, which is ultimately caused by a revert due to an InvalidSigner error. This behavior can be observed in the following Tenderly simulation:
https://www.tdly.co/shared/simulation/4b7c7025-1e4c-404d-a1f9-d38596afad9b. 
The invalid permit used in this scenario was sourced from [this GitHub issue](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory-tasks/issues/32#issuecomment-2423670546).
## Proof
As a result, signatures become invalid due to differences in the `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()`. So, the original Permit2 EIP-712 implementation verifies signature data using a domain separator different from what we expected for those permits.
Here is a test for one of these invalid permits obtained from [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/devpool-directory-tasks/issues/32#issuecomment-2423670546):
```sh
git clone https://github.com/hhio618/permit2
git checkout pay.ubq.fi/issues/363
forge test --match-test testSignatureWithDifferentDomainSeperators -vvv
```
The signature fails with the original `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR()` but works correctly with `DOMAIN_SEPARATOR_WITH_VERSION_HASH()`, which includes the `versionHash`.
## Mitigation
Perhaps the original author could resolve this by running a script to fetch these permits from the database, regenerate the correct signature, and update the relevant sections in the GitHub commit.
